declaration.negotiation_history_statement:
Hargrove Lane LLP, court-appointed interim class counsel, submits this statement in support of preliminary approval under Rule 23(e). The parties reached a binding settlement through negotiations addressing monetary relief, distribution, attorneys’ fees and expenses, and judicial oversight. Without recounting confidential mediation communications or intermediate offers, counsel clarifies that class relief and attorneys’ fees were negotiated during the same process; fees were not discussed only after class relief had been agreed upon.

The settlement requires Brightline to pay a fixed total of $30 million: $26.75 million to the class fund and a separate $3.25 million allocation for attorneys’ fees and litigation expenses, subject to court approval. Brightline has not agreed to refrain from opposing the fee request. Any portion of the fee allocation not awarded will be added to the class fund rather than returned to Brightline. Payments will be distributed automatically using existing records, without requiring class members to submit claims. Implementation, notice, and administration costs will be paid from the class fund under a transparent, court-approved budget; accordingly, the amount distributed to members will be net of those costs.

Counsel believes the settlement is fair, reasonable, and adequate to the class and warrants preliminary approval. The class fund represents approximately 41.8% of the $64 million in disputed renewal charges before administration costs and any addition of unawarded fees. Although the action survived dismissal, certification remains unresolved, success on the merits is uncertain, and trial would be approximately two to three years away. The settlement provides substantial monetary relief without those litigation risks and delays. Automatic distribution avoids a claims-filing barrier, while independent fee review and allocation of unawarded fees to the class protect class recovery.

Counsel acknowledges that concurrent negotiation of class relief and fees warrants scrutiny; the separate fee allocation alone does not establish fairness. Counsel requests that the Court evaluate the complete settlement, proposed allocation and notice procedures, administration budget, and supporting submissions under Rule 23(e), with final approval and any fee award remaining subject to the Court’s independent review.
